description: Destructive-command, secret-read and exfil rules for the Bash pre-action guard. The single source for the Claude and Codex bash guards (through lib/guard-rules.sh, generated by scripts/gen-guard-rules.py) and for the pi in-process guard.
semantics: Input is the command string. Split it on "\n" into lines, as grep reads it; a pattern matches when it matches anywhere in some line, and ^ and $ anchor at that line's start and end.
Rules run in order. A rule fires when every `match` pattern matches (each may match a different line) and no `unless` pattern matches any line.
A firing `warn` rule prints its message to stderr and evaluation continues. The first firing `deny` rule ends evaluation with its reason.
`ignore_case` folds ASCII letters only. Bytes and characters outside ASCII are never letters, digits or space.

Matching is locale-independent: the bash guards run in the C locale on bytes, and a JavaScript engine must not use Unicode-aware matching (no u or v flag), so a decision is the same on every host. A non-ASCII character such as é, U+00A0 or U+2003 is never a letter, digit or space; a command split only by U+00A0 is not split, as bash and zsh do not split it either.

`exempt` applies only for the listed engines and only to its own rule, before its patterns run. This exemption guards against accidental secret reads by agents; a deliberate same-user bypass, such as writing a script file and running it, is out of scope, as it is for every pattern guard. If any line matches a `refuse_if_line_matches` pattern, nothing is exempt. Otherwise each line is cut into simple commands at every `boundaries` character, and each simple command into blank-separated words. A simple command is exempt when its words, exactly as written, start with one of the `allowed_commands` word sequences, optionally after one `command_prefixes` word. Nothing is exempt unless every simple command on every line that has a word is exempt, nor if an exempt simple command has a word that starts with a `refuse_short_flags` flag, a word starting with - whose text after its first = holds a match of `identifier` after a character in `identifier_boundary` (or at its start), or such a match at the start of or inside the word right after a word starting with -- that has no =. Otherwise, in each simple command, every non-overlapping match of `identifier` that follows a character in `identifier_boundary` (or the start of the simple command) is replaced, left to right, by `replacement`. Everything else is kept as it was.
Engines: `claude` is the Claude Code guard; `codex` is the Codex guard, which pi runs.

Patterns use the common subset of POSIX ERE and JavaScript RegExp that scripts/gen-guard-rules.py enforces: no `.`, no backslash classes or backreferences, no POSIX [:classes:], no lookaround or lazy quantifiers, no backslash or leading ] inside brackets. Spell whitespace as [ \t\n\v\f\r].

rules.reason: Blocked destructive rm targeting absolute path, ~, $HOME, or .. — run manually if intentional.
Blocked force push — run manually if intentional.
Blocked git reset --hard without a target or on HEAD/HEAD~N/origin/* — run manually if intentional.
Blocked max/ultra effort on the sandboxless codex hatch — forbidden compound (docs/codex-routing.md §3); run at xhigh or restore the sandbox.
Blocked destructive SQL (DROP/TRUNCATE) — run manually if intentional.
Blocked DELETE FROM without WHERE — unbounded delete, run manually if intentional.

rules.message: block-destructive: .env read allowed (warn-only). Contents are now in this session's context and provider-side transcript. Don't commit session logs or memory files that capture this run.

message_by_engine.claude: block-destructive: .env read allowed (warn-only). Contents are now in this session's context and Anthropic-side transcript. Don't commit session logs or memory files that capture this run.

rules.reason: Blocked piping sensitive file (.env or /secrets/) into network tool — prompt-injection exfil vector.
Blocked curl/wget uploading sensitive file (.env or /secrets/) as body — prompt-injection exfil vector.
Blocked curl/wget with command-substituted sensitive file in body — prompt-injection exfil vector.
Blocked read under **/secrets/** — credentials must not be exposed to the agent.

exempt.why: GCP and Kubernetes resource names (projects/<n>/secrets/<name>, namespaces/<ns>/secrets/<name>) passed as arguments to read-only gcloud secrets or kubectl get/describe commands are not file reads. They are exempt only for a plain command with nothing unusual in the text: every command is one of `allowed_commands`, written literally (optionally after sudo, with no options), and the text has no quote, backslash, #, < or >. An identifier given to a flag, and any -f flag, means no exemption, and an identifier segment starting with a dot is never exempt. Every other gcloud or kubectl command (gcloud beta logging tail, kubectl exec, cp and the like) gets no exemption. To pick a resource out of gcloud or kubectl output, use their own --filter/--format (or -o jsonpath) rather than piping into grep or sed, which is denied. Before 1.4.0 the whole command was exempted when any part of it invoked gcloud or kubectl. The Codex guard never had this exemption.
